9-panel cinematic storyboard CONTACT SHEET derived from Image 1. Mix Wide, Medium, and Tight shots of the same scene.

Layout: a rigid 3x3 grid of 9 equal rectangular cells in a 16:9 landscape image. Each cell is exactly 1/3 of the width and 1/3 of the height. Separate cells with a thin black gutter.
- Content must not cross, bleed, or overlap a gutter. No collage.
- Each cell is a complete, independently framed shot — not a crop of a larger scene.

Scene: low angle, slightly below, The closed lipstick rests near the ledge edge while Scarlett (Image 2) stands beside it, reaching toward the product as wind nudges it forward., The rooftop ledge and lipstick sit in the foreground with Scarlett (Image 2)’s silhouette and glowing skyline beyond; the coral lips become the final focal point., rooftop_downtown_concrete_warm_skyline, Low late-afternoon sunlight creates warm rim light and elongated highlights around Scarlett (Image 2) and the rooftop edges. The skyline glows against a paler sky, with wind visibly affecting loose hair and grasses., Pale sky blue, warm cream, concrete gray, muted green grasses, reflective glass, charcoal clothing, and vivid coral., scarlett_city_influencer, Modern social-first product photography with tactile, editorial energy. Products shown in real-life context -- hands opening packaging, fingers pressing textures, products on bathroom shelves, kitchen counters, rumpled linen. Close-up detail shots emphasize material and finish. Flat-lays with curated minimal arrangements. Color-matched backgrounds that complement the product. Every frame feels like something you would screenshot and save

Every panel is a shot of the same scene as Image 1 — keep the characters, wardrobe, lighting, color grade, and texture consistent across all panels.

No text, dialogue bubbles, scene numbers, or watermarks.

Reference images define identity — keep every referenced character, object, and location consistent with its reference image; never render a reference image itself as a separate panel or subject.
Image 1 (primary): Primary source scene — generate 9 variant shots from this image
